messages:
linh: Heads up — nightly eval on quantized-7b-prod showed nonrepeatable outputs across runs even when we fix seed and sampling params. :eyes:
linh: I ran the harness 3x with identical config: temp=0.7, top_p=0.9, seed=42, batch_size=4. Outputs diverged after token 12.
samir: hmm, did you reuse worker processes or start fresh each run?
linh: Fresh docker containers each run. Logs show same rng init: `seed=42` in runner.log.
rafa: can you paste the minimal repro command?
linh: ```
run_eval --model quantized-7b-prod --config configs/top_p_test.yaml --seed 42 --num-seeds 1 --workers 2
```
linh: configs/top_p_test.yaml snippet:
```
sampling: {temperature: 0.7, top_p: 0.9}
batching: {max_batch_tokens: 2048}
worker: {reuse_kv_cache: false}
```
samir: did you check KV cache or prefix caching? if there's any shared state across workers that could explain it.
linh: I explicitly disabled reuse_kv_cache. worker logs show `kv_cache: disabled`.
maya: eval-runner-bot pushed a flaky CI alert earlier: "nightly-evals: instability detected for quantized-7b-prod". Could be interleaving from the sampler.
eval-runner-bot: CI alert: nightly-evals/quantized-7b-prod failed 3/10 stability checks. See: https://ci.redwood/insights/unstable-runs/quantized-7b-prod
rafa: interesting that instability aligns with top_p sampling. top_p implementation is token-level stochastic cutoff; if multiple workers handle different chunks and use different cumulative sums rounding, edge tokens could differ.
samir: that rings a bell — we had a floating point path for quantized kernels vs fp32 kernels that used different accumulation order. small fp rounding can change whether a token is included in top_p set.
linh: I repro'd with a deterministic alternative: replace top_p with top_k=50 and runs are stable across repeats. so top_p seems implicated.
maya: any quick fix idea? we need nightly stability for the eval dashboard to avoid noisy alerts.
rafa: options: 1) switch eval harness to record sampling candidate sets deterministically by sorting logits and applying a fixed tie-breaker, 2) force eval to run in single-worker mode for top_p benchmarks, or 3) run n repeats and take majority output (ugly).
samir: I'd prefer (1). Implement a deterministic top_p bit: compute cumulative probs in fp64 and break ties by (logit, token_id) fixed ordering. That should remove reduction-order nondeterminism across kernels.
linh: I'll prototype a deterministic top_p wrapper in the harness and run overnight.
linh: quick note — quantized kernels currently return logits in bf16. casting to fp64 in the harness is cheap relative to decode time, should help.
rafa: also add an eval flag `--deterministic-sampling` and make the dashboard tests opt into it for nightly stability. Keep production defaults unchanged.
maya: sounds good. Can you add a short SHARD in CI to run the deterministic path so we don't regress again? :thumbsup:
linh: will do. creating a PR now, assigning @samir and @rafa for review. thanks all.
